entries.name: relaxation-is-never-recognised
entries.claim: A candidate release that widens an already-released relation from required to optional is PLANNED, as one relaxNotNull element, rather than refused with COMPILER_STORAGE_RELATION_MUTATION_UNSUPPORTED.

kills.name: a released required relation widens through one relaxNotNull element

entries.name: widening-guard-admits-anything
entries.claim: The widening is admitted only when NOTHING ELSE about the relation moved, so the new element cannot become a channel for an unrelated mutation. Repointed after round-1 finding F1 moved the comparison from sameRelationShape's subset to the whole object.

kills.name: relation mapping fingerprints include nullability and existing physical mutations fail closed

entries.name: requiredness-leaves-the-compared-shape
entries.claim: Nullability is part of the relation shape sameRelationShape compares, so a re-tightening is REFUSED rather than riding through as a shape-identical no-op with no DDL at all.

test.namePattern: re-tightening a released relation is refused|never widened from the relation side

kills.name: relaxation is one-way: re-tightening a released relation is refused
a field-origin relation column is never widened from the relation side

entries.name: field-origin-relations-are-widened-too
entries.claim: A relation whose column originates from a field is excluded from relaxation, because that column's NOT NULL is rendered from entity.columns and a fresh install of the same release would still create it required.

test.namePattern: never widened from the relation side

kills.name: a field-origin relation column is never widened from the relation side

entries.name: old-readers-are-told-relaxation-is-transparent
entries.claim: The compatibility cell states oldRead: requiresReadFallback — a reader compiled against a required relation observes a null the moment a new writer stores one, and the matrix says so.

test.namePattern: classification axes and compatibility carve-outs are exact|widens through one relaxNotNull element

entries.name: impact-reads-only-the-new-reader
entries.claim: coexistenceImpact observes oldRead as well as newRead, so an element whose fallback burden falls on the OLD side does not publish 'none' beside a cell that says a live reader needs a fallback.

test.namePattern: classification axes and compatibility carve-outs are exact|widens through one relaxNotNull element

entries.name: migration-does-not-admit-the-new-kind
entries.claim: Migration 0022 admits relaxNotNull to north_star_internal.module_storage_elements_shape, a CHECK constraint no TypeScript build observes, and the checked-in schema snapshot records that it did.

kills.name: migrations 0006-0022 upgrade accepted G1 and converge with the checked-in snapshot

entries.name: widening-inherits-the-hand-maintained-subset
entries.claim: A relaxation is admitted only when the WHOLE relation is otherwise identical, compared as a whole object rather than through sameRelationShape's hand-maintained subset, which omits archiveBehavior. Round-1 finding F1: inheriting that subset let the compiler emit a release its own materializer refuses at PREPARE.

kills.name: a widening that also moves archiveBehavior is refused

entries.name: renderer-check-fails-open-on-unknown-kinds
entries.claim: The renderer policy check refuses a statement kind it does not recognise. Recalibrated after the round-2 review: the first mutation refused every CURRENT element kind, so it died on the admission assertion and never reached the fail-closed claim -- it proved the opposite property. This one admits ONLY the sentinel, leaving every other kind's disposition unchanged, so the unknown-kind assertion is the assertion that dies.

test.namePattern: renderer allowlist is derived from the element vocabulary

kills.name: the renderer allowlist is derived from the element vocabulary and fails closed

entries.name: provider-never-executes-the-widening
entries.claim: applyDdlElement really runs ALTER COLUMN ... DROP NOT NULL against PostgreSQL. Round-1 finding F2, and the reviewer's confirmed cheapest broken tree: the switch is not exhaustiveness-checked, so deleting the case leaves every other gate green while no DDL runs.

kills.name: a released required relation is widened by executed DDL, and a mixed live-root set is tolerated
kills.expected: managed catalog is not attributable: altered managed column

entries.name: merge-refuses-a-mixed-live-root-set
entries.claim: mergeExpectedRelations tolerates a requiredness widening between two accounted live roots. Round-1 finding F2: without an observing test, removing the branch left the compiler and provider disagreeing with every gate green, and the managed tables are tenant-shared so the refusal would fire fleet-wide.

kills.name: a released required relation is widened by executed DDL, and a mixed live-root set is tolerated
kills.expected: conflicting live roots claim managed relation
